In mathematics, '''Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates''' are coordinates for  [[Teichmüller space]] introduced by [[Werner Fenchel]] and [[Jakob Nielsen (mathematician)|Jakob Nielsen]].

==Definition==

Suppose that ''S'' is a compact [[Riemann surface]] of [[Genus (mathematics)|genus]] ''g''&nbsp;>&nbsp;1. The Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates  depend on a choice of 6''g''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;6 curves on ''S'', as follows. The Riemann surface ''S'' can be divided up into 2''g''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;2 [[pair of pants (mathematics)|pairs of pants]] by cutting along 3''g''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;3 disjoint simple closed curves. For each of these 3''g''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;3 curves γ, choose an arc crossing it that ends in other boundary components of the pairs of pants with boundary containing&nbsp;γ.

The Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates for a point of the Teichmüller space of ''S'' consist of 3''g''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;3 positive real numbers called the '''lengths''' and 3''g''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;3 real numbers called the '''twists'''. A point of Teichmüller space is represented by a hyperbolic metric on&nbsp;''S''.

The lengths of the Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates are the lengths of geodesics homotopic to  the 3''g''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;3 disjoint simple closed curves.

The twists of the Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates are given as follows. There is one twist for each of the 3''g''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;3 curves crossing one of the 3''g''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;3 disjoint simple closed curves γ. Each of these is homotopic to a curve that consists of 3 geodesic segments, the middle one of which  follows the geodesic of γ. The twist is the (positive or negative) distance the middle segment travels along the geodesic of&nbsp;γ.
